title: runs --reconcile refusal text says one run moves a dead worker's run to released, but a working key needs two runs (failed, then released)
goal: The refusal and docs that send an operator to runs --reconcile say to run it until it reports no drift (or the claim refusal names the failed state)

run: import sys; t=open('_tools/bl_land.py',encoding='utf-8').read(); bad='moves the state to released' in t; print('refusal still says one reconcile releases the run' if bad else 'ok'); sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

repro_reason: the defect is the wording of a refusal message; the two-run behaviour itself is correct, so the message text is what is wrong
notes: Review G2: bl_land.py:2279, kb/_self/coordination.md and backlog.md say runs --reconcile moves the state to released; for a working key whose worker is gone one run writes failed (bl_runs rule 2), only a second writes released (rule 4).
